agent.problem: Stop 1 has 8 story cards and only 7 choice cards.

rule.text: Choice cards are equal to or more than story cards in every stop.

agent.problem: Discovery questions make up most of the choices rather than a few. In stop 1, cards 2, 8, 13, 14 and 15 ask for details that the earlier cards do not help the baker reason out. Stop 2 does the same with cards 2, 3, 5, 6, 12 and 15. A baker who has only seen the earlier cards is largely guessing at the next detail.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: Nine of the stop's ten choice cards are multiple choice, and the only other one is true or false. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

agent.problem: The card retells the elder's Lion title from Revelation 5:5 as well as John's sight of the Lamb in Revelation 5:6, but it cites only Revelation 5:6. Its story-card range should begin at Revelation 5:5.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: The question never identifies who is singing. "Their" and "they" depend on earlier cards that are no longer on screen; the question should identify the living creatures and elders as the singers.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
